seed: At Next defaults, with no switch touched: the tutorial recording (eight seconds), the playhead three seconds in. Right click the clip, Speed > Add Speed Stop: the piece gets stops on its first frame, under the playhead and on its last frame, all at Normal, so nothing moves. The panel shows Speed stop 2 of 3, its Speed and Between stops: Ramp. Set the stop to 4x and the clip ramps from normal up to four times and back down, running 3.2 seconds instead of eight (2 x 3 / (1 + 4) + 2 x 5 / (4 + 1)), and the export is that long. Hold keeps each stretch flat (3 s at 1x, then 5 s at 4x: 4.25 s). Reset Ramp puts it back to eight seconds at one speed.

steps.comment: THE FIRST TEST: the stop is added where speed already lives, the clip's Speed submenu, at the playhead. The right click lands three eighths of the way along the eight second clip, which puts the playhead three seconds in.

steps.note: a stop on the frame under the playhead and one on each end, all at Normal: adding a stop changes nothing you can see. The panel's Time section talks about the stop: 2 of 3, its speed, and Ramp between stops

steps.comment: THE SECOND TEST: the stop at four times, picked from the panel's Speed list the way a hand opens it, by a click on its face.

steps.note: the clip ramps from normal up to four times by the stop and back down to normal at its end: eight seconds of recording in 3.2 seconds, the bar badged ramp and the playhead still on the stop's frame

steps.comment: What plays is what exports: the file runs 3.2 seconds, and a ramped stretch plays silent.
steps.name: speed-stops-ramp

steps.comment: THE THIRD TEST: the picked stop is chosen from a list too, and picking one lands the playhead on it.
THE FOURTH TEST: Hold keeps each stretch flat, three seconds at normal and five at four times.
The menu bar's Clip menu carries the same three rows under Speed.
THE FIFTH TEST: Reset Ramp puts the clip back to one speed.
